title: Human evaluation: rubrics, sampling and inter-rater agreement

videos.script: A judge grades the traffic. Something has to grade the judge, and that is people. {{people}} Two people read the same sixty replies against one sentence: does the reply address the question. {{rubric}} They agree on half of them. Chance alone would give nearly as much. Kappa, the agreement beyond chance, is zero point one one. {{v1}} Almost every disagreement is a refusal. One read the sentence as about the question, the other as answering it. {{refusal}} So they wrote the answers into the rubric, with a real reply for every rule. Kappa rises to zero point eight six. {{v2}} Then the judge, against their agreed labels. It fails every refusal, and passes every other reply. Below chance. {{judge}} Passing refusals by rule, it agrees on eighty-eight percent. And kappa is zero, because it never caught one bad reply. {{rule}} Agreement flatters. Kappa says what the judge actually sees. {{end}}
